question.text:
A real 2 × 2 matrix A has trace −2 and determinant 5. Which statement must hold for every
′
solution of v = Av?
(A) v(t) is periodic.
(B) v(t) → 0 as t → ∞.
(C) Every nonzero solution is unbounded for t > 0.
(D) v(t) is a polynomial in t.
(E) v(t) is constant.

solution.text:
2
The characteristic polynomial is λ + 2λ + 5, with roots −1 ± 2i. Both real parts are negative,
so every solution is an exponentially decaying linear combination of oscillatory terms. The
oscillations do not make the trajectories periodic because their amplitudes decay.

question.text:
A real 2 × 2 matrix has trace 0 and determinant −4. What is the dimension of the real subspace
′
of initial vectors whose solutions of v = Av tend to zero as t → ∞?
(A) 3
(B) 0
(C) 1
(D) 2
(E) It depends on the matrix.

solution.text:
2
The characteristic polynomial is λ − 4, so the distinct real eigenvalues are 2 and −2.
Only initial vectors in the one-dimensional −2 eigenspace have decaying solutions; any
component in the 2 eigenspace grows.
